NEW BUG (found and fixed this run): command-center-deps failed EACCES on a fresh named volume
environment_checks.detail: brahmadatta_command-center-node-modules is created root-owned by Docker on first use; command-center-deps runs as user 1000:1000 (the node image's non-root user) and cannot mkdir into it -- npm ci failed with EACCES. Fixed live by chowning the volume with a one-off root container (docker run --rm -v brahmadatta_command-center-node-modules:/app/node_modules alpine:3 chown -R 1000:1000 /app/node_modules) before retrying dev-up.sh. Same root-cause shape as the ARTIFACT_ROOT/evidence-volume bug fixed in the first rehearsal (named volume defaults to root ownership; non-root container can't write). Not yet fixed at the compose/Dockerfile level -- the durable fix (matching control-api.Dockerfile's own established pattern) is a follow-up, not done here for time.

environment_checks.description: NEW FINDING: model-host's backend network is internal:true by design (C4) -- it cannot pull a model from inside the running stack
environment_checks.detail: docker exec brahmadatta-model-host ollama pull codellama:7b-instruct failed: 'dial tcp: lookup registry.ollama.ai ... server misbehaving' -- expected and correct per the network's own invariant, matching the compose file's own comment ('model pulls happen explicitly on a prepared volume before the judged run'). Worked around by running a temporary, normally-networked container (brahmadatta-model-prep) mounting the SAME named volume (brahmadatta_ollama-models) to pull codellama:7b-instruct (93-98 MB/s, ~40s for 3.8GB) before handing the populated volume to the real model-host service. Not a bug -- this is the intended pre-staging workflow, but it was not written down anywhere as an operational step before this run exercised it live; worth a line in the finale runbook.

environment_checks.description: NEW FINDING: on this Docker Desktop host, a container whose ONLY network is internal:true never gets its published host port actually forwarded
environment_checks.status: worked-around, not fixed in tracked files
environment_checks.detail: docker-compose.yml's db service publishes 127.0.0.1:${POSTGRES_PORT}:5432 (D-073's mechanism for bare-metal fuzz-worker to reach Postgres) but is ONLY on the internal:true 'backend' network. HostConfig.PortBindings showed the mapping; NetworkSettings.Ports and the actual host listener stayed empty -- connection refused. Reproduced independently with a bare nginx test container on a fresh internal-only network (same failure) and a control test on a fresh non-internal network (worked). nginx's own identical-looking port publish works only because nginx also sits on the non-internal 'external' network; db has no such second network. Root cause is plausibly Docker Desktop's VM-based networking/vpnkit layer handling internal networks differently from a plain Linux dockerd (where iptables DNAT for a published port is independent of the internal flag) -- not confirmed against a real Linux finale host in this session. Workaround used for this run only, not persisted to any tracked file: `docker network connect bridge brahmadatta-db` then restart. Flagged for devops follow-up: verify on the actual finale host OS before trusting D-073's fuzz-worker-reaches-db-on-loopback assumption there.

closed_since_first_rehearsal.finding: CONFIRMED CLOSED, empirically, not just by reading code. The first rehearsal's blocker -- 'nothing in the real HTTP API, and nothing running automatically in the background, ever advances a mission past VALIDATING' -- no longer holds. With manage.py run_orchestrator running as a tick loop and manage.py run_worker (compose worker profile, kinds={BASELINE,CORRELATE,EXPORT,PATCH_GENERATE,SANITIZER_BUILD,TEARDOWN,VERIFY}) polling, a mission driven through create -> authorize -> snapshot -> preflight -> start advanced UNATTENDED and AUTOMATICALLY: VALIDATING -> BASELINE (orchestrator event: 'preflight satisfied, entering the pipeline') within one tick (~1s), the BASELINE job was claimed and actually executed by the worker (not stubbed -- it ran adapters.cpp.pipeline against the real pktcfg snapshot and produced a real, structured BASELINE_BUILD_FAILED result), and on the job's terminal FAILED result the orchestrator correctly drove BASELINE -> FAILED and ran teardown, all with zero HTTP calls after 'start'. allowed_transitions correctly went from listing BASELINE to being empty once terminal. This is real, automatic, caller-driven stage execution -- the exact gap #168 was scoped to close -- and it is closed.

unresolved_blocker_reported_not_fixed.finding: A NEW blocker, exposed only now that #168's caller-wiring gap is closed (the first rehearsal never got far enough to hit this). workers/baseline/run.py uses packages.sandbox.Jail, NOT ContainerJail, for BASELINE/SANITIZER_BUILD -- by design, per the evidence bundle's own 'isolation_mode: SUBPROCESS_JAIL' / D-049 substitution note ('The rootless-container sandbox backend (#15) is not built in this checkout'). Jail runs cmake/make/ctest as a direct subprocess of the worker PROCESS, not inside a Docker sandbox -- so the compose worker service's own image needs the C/C++ toolchain installed. It does not: brahmadatta-worker is built from control-api.Dockerfile, a Python/uvicorn-only image (confirmed directly: `cmake: not found` inside the running container). The BASELINE job for this run's mission failed in 0.034s with configure_ok=false, build_ok=false, error_code=BASELINE_BUILD_FAILED -- immediate failure consistent with a missing binary, not a real build attempt. Attempted a live workaround (apt-get install cmake build-essential inside the running worker container) and it correctly failed too: the worker container has no route off the host at all (backend network is internal:true, C4's own invariant) -- apt-get could not resolve deb.debian.org. This is the intended isolation working correctly; the fix has to be baked into the image at build time (mirroring control-api.Dockerfile's own existing runtime-stage precedent for ARTIFACT_ROOT), not patched live. This blocks every real demo scenario, including both verdicts required by this issue's acceptance criteria -- with BASELINE never producing a real pass, nothing downstream (FUZZ, PATCH_GENERATE, VERIFY, either verdict) is reachable through this compose stack as it exists today. Scoped fix: add a C/C++ toolchain (cmake, make/ninja, gcc or clang -- adapters/cpp/toolchain.py names the exact requirement) to the dev/finale target(s) of infrastructure/compose/images/control-api.Dockerfile that the compose worker service builds from, then rebuild and re-run this exact mission to confirm BASELINE passes and the pipeline reaches STRESS_TEST/FUZZ. Devops-scoped, but sized more like a real task than the small on-sight fixes in this same run -- reporting for staffing rather than attempting under this run's time budget.

both_verdicts_in_one_run.second_target_finding: demo/repositories/ contains exactly one fixture (pktcfg). It is designed to produce BOTH the Verified and Rejected verdicts required by this gate from a SINGLE target: pktcfg/patches/ ships four benchmark candidate patches -- candidate-a-correct-bounds-fix.patch (intended Verified outcome), candidate-b-rejected-crash-only-fix.patch (intended Rejected outcome, crash eliminated but test_tab_expansion regresses), plus candidate-c-compile-failure.patch and candidate-p-policy-rejected-out-of-scope.patch for the compile-gate and policy-gate paths. There is no HTTP-reachable 'operator-supplied candidate' endpoint in api/routers/ today (grepped -- none exists), so it is not yet possible to inject these fixture patches directly; PATCH_GENERATE (orchestrator/patch_generate_executor.py) only ever calls the live self-hosted model (MODEL_GATEWAY_MODE=live, no operator-supplied path wired to the API surface). This was not reachable this run regardless, since BASELINE never passed.
